title: Intervalized KV slice throttle with starvation sentinel for continuous batcher
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: continuous-batcher workloads with a mix of tiny (chat) and large (long-context) requests were still suffering intermittent starvation and p99 spikes when KV cache pinning and kernel hotpaths competed for slots. This PR implements an intervalized 'slice throttle' which splits slot reservations into short time slices and applies a starvation sentinel that temporarily deprioritizes long-running KV-heavy slices while preserving grace for in-flight small requests. Summary of changes: 1) new scheduler policy 'intervalized-slice-throttle' with configurable slice_ms and sentinel_decay_ms; 2) starvation sentinel marker in the KV admission path (soft marker, non-destructive) that influences admission probability instead of hard eviction; 3) kernel hint export for short/long slice classification to help the runtime choose attention kernels and prefetch lanes; 4) KV cache pin aging and a probabilistic decay to avoid permanent pin monopolies; 5) telemetry and opt-in feature flag under deploy/feature_flags.yaml. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2147) - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] benchmark harness runs (mixed-small-large workload) - [x] safety review for KV semantics - [x] feature-flagged rollout plan Explanation of behavior: the scheduler now splits each slot reservation window into N intervals (default 4). Each incoming request is classified into a 'slice type' based on KV usage and estimated token length; long/kv-heavy slices are admitted into later intervals and are subject to a sentinel score which decays over time if they make progress. Small requests are preferred in early intervals to reduce tail latency. Sentinel score is recorded as a soft tag on admission metadata and is used by the admission sampler rather than being an eviction signal, so no extra cache churn is introduced. Kernel hints are emitted to the runtime via the existing kernel_hints API to switch to low-latency attention kernels for early-interval small requests. Testing and results: lab benchmarks show 15% reduction in p99 generation latency on mixed workloads, 7% higher aggregate throughput under steady-state, and 2x fewer KV-cache thrashing events in the replayed production trace. We ran a 48h canary with the feature flag enabled at 10% traffic and observed no regression in correctness or error-rate. Rollout plan: behind feature flag off by default; stage to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring alarms on p50/p95/p99, KV eviction rate, and allocation failures. Related: ENG-2210 contains the follow-up plan for heuristic tuning and adaptive slice sizing.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial implementation of intervalized throttle and sentinel (interval_throttle.go, kv_sentinel.go); add kernel hint plumbing and tests; docs and feature flag. Commit messages: feat(scheduler): add intervalized slice throttle; feat(kv): add starvation sentinel tagging; perf(runtime): emit kernel hints for slice classes; test: integration harness for mixed workloads; docs: interval throttle overview.
review_comments: Liam: asked for clearer guardrails around sentinel decay and whether it could starve long running analytical jobs; response: sentinel is probabilistic and decays with progress, added extra unit tests and a knob sentinel_decay_ms and max_deprioritize_pct. Mateo: requested metrics for 'sentinel_hits' and an SLI proposal; added metrics and a dashboard template. Chen: asked to ensure kernel hint path is opt-in in case of future kernel churn; we added a runtime flag and a safe fallback path. Several small nit and style requests addressed. Final review approved after 2 iteration of changes.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in intervalized scheduling policy to reduce tail latency for mixed workloads. Default behavior is disabled; enabling may reduce p99 at the cost of slightly longer latency for very large KV-heavy requests. Provides knobs for slice duration, sentinel decay, and kernel-hinting. Backwards compatible when feature flag is off.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flagged rollout recommended. Watch metrics: batcher.p99_ms, batcher.p95_ms, kv.eviction_rate, scheduler.sentinal_hits, runtime.kernel_hint_switches. Suggested canary: 10% for 24h, then 50% for 24-48h, then full rollout if metrics stable. If regressions observed, toggle feature flag off and revert via rollout dashboard.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover sentinel scoring and probabilistic admission; integration tests simulate mixed small/large request traces and verify fairness and non-starvation; benchmark harness run on m60 cluster with representative production trace; results captured in docs/engineering/batcher/benchmarks-2026-02-18.md.
additional_context: This PR is part of a broader effort to decouple admission pacing and kernel selection from pure slot accounting so that we can optimize for end-to-end latency rather than per-token throughput alone. Follow-ups include adaptive slice sizing and ML-powered sentinel thresholds (ENG-2210).
